concurrency_mechanism: worker thread pool size, set with the `--worker-thread` flag on `kestra server standalone` (one Kestra worker thread runs one task at a time)
notes: Same shape and workload as process/sleep but on Kestra's stock task runner for script tasks, io.kestra.plugin.scripts.runner.docker.Docker with containerImage python:slim, which creates a volume and a container per task and removes both afterwards. Second data point for what container-per-task costs at concurrency. Concurrency is still exactly 20; the worker threads are simply blocked waiting on the single Docker daemon. Compare the per-task window (RUNNING -> SUCCESS) against the serial container lifecycle measured on the same box, in kestra_runtime.json serial_docker_baseline.

sanity.how: the harness refuses a rep unless all 100 executions report SUCCESS and exactly 2000 unit task runs each carry CREATED, RUNNING and SUCCESS timestamps
sanity.concurrency_derivation: interval sweep over every unit task run's RUNNING -> SUCCESS window

cpu_sampler_note: cpu.* is sampled host-wide every 0.5s from /proc/stat and /proc/*/comm. busy_cores_p50 is cores busy across the whole box (Kestra JVM + Postgres + task processes). python_procs counts any process whose comm starts with python3, so it includes the harness itself and overcounts by 1; cpucheck_process_cpu.json has the filtered per-process accounting.
